subject.title: fix(telegram): Allow multi-agent ACP bindings within same account

question: Should Telegram support multiple simultaneous ACP session bindings for one account/topic, or only a same-account ownership handoff?
rationale: The PR description promises independent same-topic bindings, but the branch implements last-writer-wins; changing that model affects routing, list/unbind behavior, and session-state expectations.

options.title: Require True Simultaneous Bindings
options.body: Rework the binding data model and tests so multiple targetSessionKeys for the same account/topic remain addressable, while preserving plugin-state storage and cross-account rejection.

options.title: Accept Same-Account Handoff
options.body: Treat the behavior as an explicit ownership switch, update the PR description/tests/proof accordingly, and do not claim independent bindings.

options.title: Pause This Direction
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it until a narrower maintainer-owned binding-model design exists.

recommendation.title: Require True Simultaneous Bindings
recommendation.body: Rework the binding data model and tests so multiple targetSessionKeys for the same account/topic remain addressable, while preserving plugin-state storage and cross-account rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history across thread-binding persistence and migration files, which makes him the best available owner for the binding-model decision.
